title: Ada and the Garden
premise: Lena Nakamura's ledgers record the guild's trades in impossible things: years of life, borrowed names, doors to countries that were erased from maps. When the old gods resume answering prayers, every debt in her books comes due at once, and Lena discovers her own name on a page she never wrote — sold before her birth by an ancestor who bargained with a dying god. To escape, she must find the Door of Ada, the last gate out of Vessany, a country that no longer exists except inside the garden where the gods were buried. The guildmaster means to keep the door shut and hoard the gods' returning power for himself; opening it will unmake him but also erase everything written about Vessany, including Lena's memories. In the end she rewrites her own ledger entry — trading her inheritance of memory for the country's freedom — and walks out through the garden carrying only one thing: her own name, hers at last.
about_author: Silas Joubert is a former archivist from the coastal town of Port Meridian who spent a decade cataloguing merchant guild records before turning to fiction. His novels are known for their ledger-precise prose and their obsession with what paperwork can hold of a soul.

chapters.title: The Weight of Ink
chapters.summary: Lena Nakamura, POV. A night shift in the guildhall: Lena balances entries for traded years and borrowed names while creditors circle her own debt-contract. She finds one page that resists her pen — an entry that rewrites itself. Emotional beat: weary competence cracking into unease as the impossible intrudes on the mundane.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. Word spreads through the city that the old gods are answering prayers again; a beggar's wish heals his daughter, and the guild scrambles to claim credit. The guildmaster, Corvane Ash, orders all god-related debts flagged. Beat: awe curdling into dread as Lena realizes her ledgers are now the most dangerous documents alive.

chapters.title: A Debt in Someone Else's Hand
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. Investigating the self-rewriting page, Lena finds her own name listed as collateral on a contract dated sixty years before her birth, signed by a grandmother she never knew. Beat: vertigo — her identity was never entirely hers, and someone has been holding it in trust.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Garden
chapters.summary: Corvane, POV. Corvane tours the sealed garden behind the guildhall where the old gods were buried after the fall of Vessany, feeling them stir beneath the soil. He plans to harvest their returning power alone. Beat: cold ambition; the reader sees the antagonist's vision is genuinely seductive.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Won't Say
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. Lena bribes a retired scribe, Aunt Iyo, who reveals the guild once served as priests of Vessany and the ledgers were prayer-books first. The Door of Ada is real — and it opens only for someone named in the founding ledger. Beat: revelation reframing everything Lena thought her work was.

chapters.title: Small Gods, Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Tomas, POV. Tomas, a guild runner and Lena's only friend, delivers a petition to a shrine and watches a minor god answer — then demand payment in memories. He barely escapes with his childhood intact. Beat: wonder turned to horror; the gods' return is not salvation but collection.

chapters.title: Audited
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. Corvane confronts Lena with evidence she copied forbidden pages, offering partnership: help him bind the gods' power into the ledgers, or be sold against her own contract. Beat: coercion dressed as opportunity; Lena accepts with a hidden resolve forming.

chapters.title: The Founding Page
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. In the vault, Lena reads the founding ledger: her grandmother didn't sell her — she hid her, writing Lena's name into the Door's covenant so no god or guildman could claim her outright. Beat: grief and gratitude braided together; inheritance revealed as protection, not betrayal.

chapters.title: Rust and Roses
chapters.summary: Lena and Tomas, alternating. They breach the garden wall at night and find it impossibly vast inside — rows of graves, each growing a different flower, each flower humming with a sleeping god. Beat: eerie beauty; the sacred made physical and close.

chapters.title: The God Who Was Buried Twice
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. At the garden's center stands Ada's grave, empty except for a mirror. Her reflection speaks: Ada never died; she became the door itself, waiting for a scribe honest enough to open her. Beat: intimate uncanniness; the quest acquires a voice and a condition.

chapters.title: Terms of Collection
chapters.summary: Corvane, POV. The gods begin collecting on the guild's centuries of unpaid spiritual debt; senior guild members age decades overnight. Corvane doubles down, planning to sacrifice the debtors' names to buy himself divinity. Beat: power's corruption accelerating; the villain becomes desperate and more dangerous.

chapters.title: Everything We Wrote Down
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. Lena learns the cost of opening Ada's door: Vessany exists now only as writing, and opening the door will burn every text of it — including her grandmother's letters and her own memories of learning to read here. Beat: the true price named; desire and loss locked together.

chapters.title: The Runners' Riot
chapters.summary: Tomas, POV. Debt-collecting gods spark panic; runners and scribes riot when they learn the guild has been trading their names for generations. Tomas organizes them toward the garden, making the mob a force Lena must steer, not flee. Beat: righteous fury; the personal becomes collective.

chapters.title: A Bargain With Teeth
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. Lena offers Corvane a trade: her grandmother's hidden covenant page in exchange for releasing her contract. He agrees, then betrays her instantly, seizing both pages and locking her in the vault. Beat: bitter lesson — you cannot out-ledger a man who owns the ledger house.

chapters.title: Ink and Blood
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. Imprisoned among the ledgers, Lena discovers ink made from Ada's grave-soil responds to intent, not authority. She writes herself free — literally editing the vault lock's entry — and understands the founding truth: scribes were always the gods' counterweight. Beat: empowerment earned through craft, not force.

chapters.title: The Garden Opens Its Eyes
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The gods rise fully as Corvane begins his rite; the city's sky fills with names being called in. Tomas holds the mob at the wall, buying Lena time. Beat: apocalyptic pressure; every thread converging on the garden.

chapters.title: Coronation of Ash
chapters.summary: Corvane, POV. Mid-rite, Corvane takes the gods' power and briefly becomes something vast — then the collected debts arrive at once, and divinity begins eating him alive from the inside. Beat: tragic climax of corruption; he gets exactly what he wanted and it unmakes him.

chapters.title: The Door of Ada
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. Lena reaches the mirror-grave as Corvane collapses. Ada asks the final question: what will you carry? Lena chooses her own name over her memories of Vessany, signs the closing entry in grave-ink, and pushes the door open. Beat: sacrificial clarity; the theme of inheritance resolved by renunciation.

chapters.title: A Country, Unwritten
chapters.summary: Lena and Tomas, alternating. Vessany dissolves gently — streets becoming light, the dead going home — while refugees stream through the door into the world beyond maps. Lena feels her memories thinning like morning fog. Beat: elegiac release; grief and liberation indistinguishable.

chapters.title: Blank Pages
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. On the far side, Lena wakes with almost nothing: no homeland, no grandmother's face, only skills and one word — her name. Tomas stays beside her, promising to remember enough for both of them. Beat: tender aftermath; love as external memory.

chapters.title: The New Ledger
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. Refugees ask Lena to keep records of what they carry out of Vessany — stories, recipes, grudges, songs. She opens a fresh book and writes the first entry honestly, for free. Beat: quiet rebirth; the scribe's vocation transformed from bondage to gift.

chapters.title: Ada and the Garden
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. Years later, Lena tends a small garden behind the new settlement where one flower hums faintly — Ada, resting, not gone. Lena writes the final line of the old ledger and closes it forever. Beat: peaceful closure; memory outlives nations when kept by choice, not contract.
